Fatty liver disease rising in U.S. kids as ultraprocessed diets surge
sources.text: Schwimmer Lab Welcome to the Schwimmer Lab The Schwimmer Lab at UC San Diego is a leader in clinical and translational research on metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD, as known as Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease or NAFLD) in children, young adults, and families. Our team includes five pediatric gastroenterologists working with collaborators in many other fields of medicine (endocrinology, pediatrics, psychology, radiology), and science (chemistry, genomics, microbiome, nutrition, public health). Our goal is to improve the diagnosis and treatment of Pediatric MASLD in order to promote the health and quality of life of children, adolescents, and young adults with MASLD. Our team has made many important discoveries about MASLD in children. We established the prevalence and incidence of MASLD in children. We discovered the different types of liver injury that can occur in children with MASLD. We evaluated genes that predisposed to MASLD and are associated with the severity of the liver injury. We demonstrated the relationship between MASLD and many other health problems including type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, osteoporosis, and depression. We contributed to advances in MRI measurement of liver fat and liver fibrosis. We conducted clinical trials of nutritional interventions as well as medications for the treatment of MASLD. We will continue to make advances to support improvements in the care and outcomes of children, adolescents, and young adults with MASLD. sources.text: Contact Us Mailing Address 200 West Arbor Drive, Mail Code 7450 San Diego, CA 92103 This address is for letter mail only. Contact us for shipping instructions for packages. Lab Contacts Jeffrey Schwimmer, MD Principal Investigator (619) 543-5226 jschwimmer@health.ucsd.edu Amy Alba Program and Fiscal Coordinator (619) 543-5226 amalba@health.ucsd.edu Volunteer Opportunities The Schwimmer Lab is currently accepting volunteer applications from UC San Diego undergraduate sophomores and juniors with an interest in research or healthcare. No lab or research experience is necessary. We value all work, volunteer, and class experience from your college career. Tasks will be primarily administrative in nature and support clinical research projects with opportunities for additional projects based on student interest. The volunteer commitment is 4–8 hours per week for one year. Please check the REAL portal, as our position will be posted in late September.

sources.text: Faculty Labs The Department of Pediatrics at UC San Diego is one of the nation's premier Departments devoted to improving the understanding of disease pathogenesis in order to better diagnose, treat and prevent diseases in infants and children. Research efforts include basic and clinical science in various fields spanning the whole range of maladies. Another important goal in the Department is to build and foster the development of the next generation of research leaders in Pediatric Medicine. There has been no better time for research and training in Pediatrics than what is currently and what we predict it will be in the next decade!
